name: Analogy & Metaphor Standardization
description: Examines the semantic originality, cliché alignment, and structural predictability of analogies and similes.
mechanism: To explain complex topics safely and understandably, generative AI draws heavily upon a statistically normalized pool of analogies. Because the AI is optimized to be helpful and avoid confusing the user, it gravitates toward universally understood, albeit completely overused, comparisons ('like a symphony orchestra', 'like a well-oiled machine', 'like finding a needle in a haystack'). Human creativity frequently generates analogies that are idiosyncratic, culturally hyper-specific, or slightly messy but highly evocative. This tool extracts all comparative figures of speech (similes, metaphors, analogies) and maps their semantic drift against a vast database of known clichés and highly probable corporate metaphors. An extremely tight clustering of 'safe, highly predictable' analogies flags forced algorithmic simplification.
parameters:
Analysis: High-Dimensional Semantic Embedding & Figure of Speech Extraction
Metric: Metaphor Predictability & Cliché Alignment Proximity
Output: 0-100 Figurative Sterility Score
accuracy: Moderate-High — 75-82%, though it acts as a strong filter for 'low-effort text' regardless of whether the origin is human or machine.
source: Cognitive linguistics and computational metaphor identification research.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated educational content, motivational posts, or B2B copy that relies on tired, perfectly engineered, yet soulless metaphors.
strengths:
• Directly exposes the 'safe homogenization' of AI creativity caused by RLHF alignment.
• Outperforms simple n-gram detection because it evaluates the semantic space of the metaphor, not just the exact wording.
• Exceptional against 'thought leadership' posts on social media that attempt to sound profound using standard corporate imagery.
limitations:
• Humans writing highly generic, low-effort copy (like SEO marketing farm workers) score identically to AI, causing false positives.
• Computationally expensive; requires high-dimensional vector space mapping to evaluate metaphor originality.
• Completely blind to texts that are purely informational and do not utilize figurative language.

references.title: Beigman Klebanov, B. et al. (2016). Semantic classifications for detection of verb metaphors. ACL.
